$comment: Each row is one deliberate defect. tools/mutate.js applies it to a throwaway copy of the repository and runs the full suite. A mutation that still passes is a SURVIVOR and fails the build; a `find` that no longer matches exactly once is STALE and also fails, because it means the code moved and the row stopped describing anything. M44 was written and REMOVED as an equivalent mutation, not as a coverage hole: with no insertion at all, every record lands in the unindexed fallback and is still delivered, so the pass is slower and nothing is wrong. M43 (a one-metre AABB) is the row that proves the index is actually consulted, and it is killed.

mutations.replace: if false then
mutations.why: Never answer from the cache, so every require re-runs the module and hands back a FRESH table. Anything with state in it -- an id counter, a rate limiter window, an LRU -- is then duplicated per caller, and two callers holding "the same module" hold two of them.

mutations.find: if not bucket or now - bucket.started >= windowMs then
mutations.replace: if not bucket or now - bucket.started >= (windowMs / 1000) then
mutations.why: Treat the window as SECONDS while the clock is still GetGameTimer MILLISECONDS, which is the exact mistake 5.2 warns about in a comment: every rate limit on the server becomes a thousand times looser, silently, and nothing logs. The plan says the security limiter and CisRate differ, and rate.lua itself says they differ "in ONE thing that matters -- what happens at the window boundary". They differ in three, and the unit is one of them. A reader who believed that header would write exactly this row, which is why the comparison against CisRate is pinned in contracts.

mutations.find: if not bucket and (rateCounts[src] or 0) >= RATE_BUCKET_CAP then
mutations.replace: if not bucket and (rateCounts[src] or 0) >= 100000000 then
mutations.why: Raise the per-source bucket cap out of reach. Event names arrive off the wire, so an unbounded map is a memory growth rate a client controls: one source sending a few hundred thousand distinct event names would grow the table without limit, and the resource that reads it -- a server under attack -- is the one paying.

mutations.replace:
-- the refusal removed: Cis.player.ped is absent on the server again, and
-- calling it from a server-side consumer is "attempt to call a nil value".
function Cis.player.ped()
    return nil
end
mutations.why: Answer nil instead of `false, 'client only'` for the opposite realm. This is the silent no-op the original comment was arguing against, and it is worse than the raise it replaced: a raise names itself in the console and sends someone to look, while a nil is indistinguishable from "the player has no vehicle" and is silently absorbed by every caller that treats nil as data. The contract suite scans init.lua and would report the refusal missing, and E070 reports the same absence as a missing stub. Two gates, one defect: the second was added with the rule, and `check: api` is what puts the mutation runner in a position to see it.

mutations.find:
local function sweepExits(coords)
    for id in pairs(inside) do
mutations.replace:
local function sweepExits(coords)
    -- M72: departures are left to the candidate query, which cannot see a point
    -- the player has walked clear of.
    return
    for id in pairs(inside) do
mutations.why: Stop sweeping the points the player is inside, leaving departure to the grid candidate query. The candidate box is centred on the POINT, not the player, so a player who walks away from a point is no longer a candidate and the point never fires onExit -- a point that can be entered and never left. The 7.1 test that steps the player well clear is the only one that sees it; a test that merely crosses the boundary still passes, because the point is still a candidate there.

mutations.find:
request(spec.requestArgs(hash or name))
    else
        request(hash or name)
    end
mutations.replace:
else
        -- M73: the and/or form. A call in the middle of an
        -- "a and f(p, q) or b" is truncated to its first value, so the
        -- streamed flag never reaches RequestStreamedTextureDict.
        request(spec.requestArgs and spec.requestArgs(hash or name) or (hash or name))
    end
mutations.why: Restore the `spec.requestArgs and spec.requestArgs(x) or x` form that this branch replaced. In `a and f(p, q) or b` a call in the middle is truncated to its FIRST value, so the streamed flag is never passed. The native then reads a nil where a BOOL belongs -- which is false -- and quietly requests a NON-streamed dictionary. It compiles, lints, and is correct on the six kinds whose request native takes one argument, so nothing else in the file notices. The 7.2 test that COUNTS the arguments is the only thing that sees it, which is why this row counts too: the first attempt at it renamed the branch but kept the correct call, and the runner reported it as a survivor -- a row that describes no defect is worth catching as loudly as one the suite misses.

mutations.find:
local contractOk, contractReason = checkContract(slot, contract)
    if not contractOk then
        return false, contractReason
    end
mutations.replace:
local contractOk, contractReason = checkContract(slot, contract)
    if not contractOk and false then
        return false, contractReason
    end
mutations.why: Stop enforcing a provider DECLARED contract. The doc promised this argument since CIS_LIBS_API_CONTRACT.md §3 and no code implemented it, so a provider passing { api=1, requiredMethods={...} } believed itself checked while it was silently ignored. This is what happens if it regresses: a provider demanding a method the slot does not declare registers successfully and then answers nil to every caller for the life of the process.

mutations.find:
if type(method) ~= 'string' then
                return false, ('contract.requiredMethods entries must be strings, got %s')
                    :format(type(method))
            end
mutations.why: Drop the string check on requiredMethods entries. A non-string entry then reaches the slot lookup, declared[method] with a table key answers nil, and the provider is refused with a message naming a TABLE rather than the field -- or, if the key collides with a real method, it passes validation on a contract nobody wrote.

mutations.find: local recorded = contract or (held and held.contract) or nil
mutations.replace: local recorded = contract or nil
mutations.why: Lose the contract on a bare re-registration. A provider restarting its resource re-registers with no contract, the recorded promise is dropped, and cis_libs goes back to enforcing nothing. This is the same defect as never having had a contract, and it appears at exactly the moment a provider is least able to notice -- a resource restart.

mutations.find:
return false, ('capability %q has no method %q; declared methods are %s')
                    :format(slot, method, table.concat(sortedMethodNames(slot), ', '))
mutations.replace:
return false, ('capability %q has no method %q')
                    :format(slot, method)
mutations.why: Shorten the refusal so it no longer lists what the slot DOES declare. The message still says which method was wrong, but an operator staring at a framework slot with eleven methods has to go and read shared/registry.lua to learn the eleven real names. A refusal that does not say its own fix generates a support thread.

mutations.find: local PENDING = 0
mutations.replace: local PENDING = 2
mutations.why: Treat GetShapeTestResultIncludingMaterial's DONE value (2) as pending. 1 and 2 both mean done; 0 is the only pending state. Treating 2 as pending makes a resolved probe look unfinished until the timeout, so every hit becomes a timeout.

mutations.find: RegisterKeyMapping(handle.command, options.description or name, mapper or 'keyboard', key or '')
mutations.replace: RegisterKeyMapping(name, options.description or name, mapper or 'keyboard', key or '')
mutations.why: Register the mapping against the bare name instead of +name. RegisterKeyMapping's first argument is the command string the engine fires; without the plus, the +name command we registered is never the one the key runs, so the binding appears in the settings menu and does nothing.

mutations.find: if restricted and src ~= 0 then
mutations.replace: if false then
mutations.why: Skip the ACE check on a restricted command. RegisterCommand's restricted flag is one half; without this, a source that reached the handler -- a console that forwards a src, or a restricted flag the platform did not honour -- runs as anyone.

mutations.find:
if IsDuplicityVersion() then
        return id
    end
mutations.replace:
if not IsDuplicityVersion() then
        return id
    end
mutations.why: Wait for the entity on the SERVER and skip the wait on the client. That is the inverted realm: the client is the one whose entity may not have streamed in, and a handler that then calls GetEntityCoords raises.

mutations.find:
nativeNotify(text)
    return true
mutations.replace: return true
mutations.why: Skip the native GTA feed when no ui provider is registered. Notify then answers true and shows nothing -- the same silent no-op the ui slot exists to prevent, and the 7.9 test that counts BeginTextCommandThefeedPost is the thing that sees it.

mutations.find:
local function noProvider()
    return false, 'no ui provider'
end
mutations.replace:
local function noProvider()
    return true
end
mutations.why: Make progress/confirm/input succeed without a ui provider. Those three forward only and answer false, 'no ui provider' without one -- a true here is a fake dialog that never ran, and every caller waiting on confirm hangs or proceeds as if the player agreed.

mutations.find: EndTextCommandDisplayHelp(0, true, false, -1)
mutations.replace: EndTextCommandDisplayHelp(0, false, false, -1)
mutations.why: Draw help text with loop=false. The native then flashes once and vanishes, so isOpen stays true while nothing is on screen. Native help must stay until hide; loop=true is the documented way (natives_gta.json END_TEXT_COMMAND_DISPLAY_HELP).

mutations.find:
if value ~= nil and value ~= false then
            return value
        end
mutations.replace:
if value ~= nil then
            return value
        end
mutations.why: Treat false as success. A predicate `return loaded` that is still false then returns immediately, and the wait never waits. The 7.8 test that polls false twice then answers is the thing that sees it.

mutations.find:
return nil, ('waitFor timed out after %dms'):format(timeout)
                .. (msg and (' (' .. tostring(msg) .. ')') or '')
mutations.replace:
error(('waitFor timed out after %dms'):format(timeout)
                .. (msg and (' (' .. tostring(msg) .. ')') or ''), 2)
mutations.why: Raise on timeout. Callers that cannot wrap the wait in pcall then crash a thread, and the 7.8 test that pcalls a timeout and requires it NOT to raise is the thing that sees it.

mutations.find: timeout = 10000
mutations.replace: timeout = 1000
mutations.why: Default the timeout to 1000. The api.lua contract says 10000, and a caller who writes waitFor(fn) expecting ten seconds gets one. The 7.8 test that lets the default run and asserts the clock crossed 10000 is the thing that sees it.

mutations.find: lockState = GetVehicleDoorLockStatus(vehicle),
mutations.replace: lockState = nil,
mutations.why: Drop lockState from the getter. A garage that round-trips properties then leaves every door unlocked or locked wrongly. The 7.10 test that reads lockState is the thing that sees it.

mutations.find:
for i = 0, 7 do
        if not IsVehicleWindowIntact(vehicle, i) then
mutations.replace:
for i = 0, 7 do
        RollUpWindow(vehicle, i)
        if not IsVehicleWindowIntact(vehicle, i) then
mutations.why: Roll up every window while reading properties. A getter that mutates the vehicle is not a getter, and a player whose windows were down has them slammed shut by a sync snapshot. The 7.10 test that counts RollUpWindow is the thing that sees it.

mutations.find: if live.opts.schema ~= nil then
mutations.replace: if live.opts.schema ~= nil and false then
mutations.why: Skip the schema check. A client can then send count=999999 or a string where a table belongs and the handler still runs. 7.11 exists so a typed payload is a boundary, not a comment.
Accept any series name. GetDiagnostics.timings would then grow keys 8.2 cannot attribute, and a typo in observe() would look like a missing pass.
